People Ops: Thanks for dropping questions after today's all-hands. We'll answer live here for anything about reviews, leveling, promos, comp, benefits, or the calibration process. :wave:

Nina P: Two quick ones: 1) Are managers required to attach objective metrics for promotion requests? 2) How does the PIP process interact with leveling?

People Ops: Good Qs. 1) Yes, attach at least two concrete evidence items (OKRs, adoption metrics, project outcomes, or shipped customer features). The comp committee prefers measurable impact. 2) PIPs are separate from promotion eligibility. If someone is on a PIP, a promotion is generally paused until successful completion; exceptions are rare and need exec sign-off.

Tom H: If someone was overlooked last cycle (manager admits they should've promoted), what's the fastest path to correct?

People Ops: Start with a manager-requested retro promo: short justification + timeline + peer feedback. We'll route to comp committee for expedited review. Payroll retro pay possible when approved. Expect ~2 week turnaround for fast-track cases.

Nina P: Will calibration be anonymized? Concern about bias when names come up early.

Maya (CTO): We're doing an anonymized first-pass: managers submit anonymized evidence and a neutral summary. Names are revealed only when necessary to resolve ties or exceptions.

Tom H: Can managers see market comp data when recommending out-of-cycle market adjustments?

Luis (CFO): Yes, comp partners will provide benchmark data. Managers should include a short business case and any external offers if available. Out-of-cycle increases are for retention or critical hires and require approval.

PeopleOps Bot: Promo template reminder: 1) Summary (1 line), 2) Top 3 impact bullets, 3) Evidence links, 4) Proposed effective date, 5) Manager recommendation. Template: https://intranet.redwood.example/promo-template

People Ops: We'll synthesize this thread into an FAQ and add examples of "scale vs scope" to the rubric doc. If you need private help, book office hours: https://calendar.redwood.example/peopleops-officehours. Thanks! :thumbsup:
